newsitem.title: USA: Clinton announces design of World War II memorial.
newsitem.headline: Clinton announces design of World War II memorial.

text.p: A vast collonaded plaza at the east end of a reflecting pool between the Lincoln Memorial and the Washington Monument will be erected to honour World War II service and sacrifice, President Clinton said Friday.

Clinton unveiled the plan for the World War II memorial, which was authorised by Congress in 1993, at a White House ceremony at which he also presented the Presidential Medal of Freedom to former Sen. Bob Dole.

Designed by Austrian-born architect Friedrich St. Florian, former dean of the Rhode Island School of Design, the monument will be built on a 7.4 acre site in the park in the centre of official Washington known as the Mall.

Clinton said it would commemorate "one of the great defining passages in our nation's history," and added that it was fitting that it would be flanked by monuments to George Washington, hero of the U.S. Revolution, and Abraham Lincoln, who preserved the union during the Civil War.
"For if the Revolutionary War marks the birth of our republic and the Civil War its greatest trial, then surely America's triumph in World War II will forever signal our coming of age," Clinton said.
He said the memorial, to be dedicated on Veteran's Day in the year 2000, would remember the heroics and hardships of Americans on the homefront as well as those who fought.
